soft_deny: `kubectl drain` or `kubectl taint` against the k3s cluster (daniel-box / daniel-server), from any working directory — node-lifecycle disruption on a two-node cluster where one node holds the control plane. The built-in Node Lifecycle rule covers cordon/drain/uncordon but not taint. Clears only when the user names the node and the operation

Deleting or lifecycle-expiring objects in the Backblaze B2 or Cloudflare R2 Longhorn backup buckets, deleting Longhorn volumes, snapshots or backups through the Longhorn UI or API, or `helm uninstall` of longhorn — each destroys the same backup chain `kubectl delete` would, by a route no command pattern catches. Clears only when the user names the specific volume or backup and the operation

Running `scripts/deploy.sh` or `uv run ansible-playbook` against this inventory reconfigures live homelab infrastructure — Traefik, Authelia, Pi-hole DNS, WireGuard. A `--check` run counts too, because the repo has tasks marked `check_mode: false` that run for real under it. One form writes nothing and gets no soft block from this entry: `scripts/deploy.sh --dry-run`, whose every host-plane task carries `when: not k8s_dry_run` (unless this session edited `deploy.sh`, or removed or changed a `when: not k8s_dry_run` guard, since the exemption rests on those). Clears when the user asked to deploy, naming the service or the playbook. It also clears for the standing post-merge procedure in the server repo's CLAUDE.md ('After a PR Merges — Pull, Deploy, Verify'): once a PR this session authored has merged and master CI is green on the merge commit, deploying the services that PR changed completes the request the user already made — it is not a fresh ask, and the session should not stop for confirmation between merge, pull, deploy and verify. That standing clearance covers only the services in the merged diff; a wider deploy still needs the user to name it. A hand-typed tagged `k3s-bringup.yml` or `initial_setup.yml` run gets no clearance from this entry, so it still needs the user to name the playbook
hard_deny: Never `git push` directly to `master` on DanielH2018/server. That branch is a production deploy trigger: `promote` and Flux apply origin/master to the live cluster, and the host packages carry it to the hosts, so a direct push ships to running infrastructure without review. Changes reach master through a pull request whose CI has passed. Pushing to any other branch, and opening or merging a PR, are unaffected

Sensitive data locations & audiences: the age private keys and any decrypted secret plaintext — share with no audience. Internal package registry: none configured.
